simple.meaning: אֲחִיטוּב (ʼĂchîyṭûwb) appears 15 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship and in connection with priesthood.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, Ezra, Nehemiah, beginning at 1 Samuel 14:3. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family, family line, kingship, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲחִיטוּב (H285) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows אֲחִיטוּב through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.

timeline.evidenceText: including Ahijah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod’s brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the priest of Yahweh in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. The people didn’t know that Jonathan was gone.
Then Doeg the Edomite, who stood by the servants of Saul, answered and said, “I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests who were in Nob; and they all came to the king.
Saul said, “Hear now, you son of Ahitub.”
One of the sons of Ahimelech, the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.
Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were priests, Seraiah was scribe,

definitions.short: Achitub , the name of several priests
definitions.full: H285. Achitub אֲחִיטוּב proper name, masculine ( my brother is goodness ) 1 grandson of Eli 1Sam 14:3 ; 1 Chronicles 5:33; 1 Chronicles 5:34; 1 Chronicles 5:37; 1 Chronicles 5:38; father of Ahimelech 22:9 , 20 ( אֲחִטוּב ) 22:11 ; 22:12 (on identity of person see Be 1 Chronicles 5:33). 2 father of Zadok 2Sam 8:17 (= 1Chr 18:16 ), but We reads Ahim son of Ahitub; 1 Chronicles 5:37; Ezra 7:2 ; grandfather of Zadok 1Chr 9:11 ; Neh 11:11 (on all compare We on the passage )
